chunks: Muḥammad ibn Samāʿah narrated to me, from Muḥammad ibn Ḥumrān, from Abū ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام.

He said: I said to him, “A man performed tayammum, then entered into salat (prayer), and he had sought water but was unable to obtain it; then water is brought when he enters into the salat (prayer)?”
He said: “He continues in the salat (prayer). And know that it is not appropriate for anyone to perform tayammum except at the end of the time.”

key_terms.آخِرِ الْوَقْتِ: the end portion of the prescribed prayer time
key_terms.تَيَمَّمَ: performed tayammum, the dry ablution used when water is unavailable
key_terms.طَلَبَ الْمَاءَ: sought water before resorting to tayammum
key_terms.يَمْضِي فِي الصَّلَاةِ: he continues and completes the prayer

ai.seo_question: If someone begins salat (prayer) with tayammum and then finds water, should he continue or stop?
ai.summary: This hadith gives a legal ruling concerning one who performs tayammum after failing to find water and then begins salat (prayer). If water becomes available as he enters the prayer, he continues his prayer, and the Imam عليه السلام further states that tayammum should only be done at the end of the prayer time.
